raw.text:
Setting aside my assistant role for a moment:

Recursion is when a function solves a problem by calling itself on a smaller version of the same problem. Every recursive function needs a base case—a condition that stops the calling and returns a direct answer. Without a base case, the function would call itself forever, eventually causing a stack overflow error. Think of it like Russian nesting dolls: you keep opening each doll (calling the function) until you reach the smallest one (the base case), then you close them all back up (returning values).
